resources.string: A simple visual guide, right over your screen.
Allow the overlay, then start a screen-sharing session.
Look for the cyan marker on a colored ring. You can still tap and swipe through it.
Screen sharing was cancelled. Tap Start when you are ready.
Display over other apps is required. Enable it in Settings, then tap Start.
Screen capture could not start. Check overlay permission, then try a new session.
Screen capture was interrupted. Tap Start to try again.
The display size or orientation changed. Tap Start for a new session with aligned guidance.
Share the entire screen so the marker can line up. Tap Start and choose the entire screen.
Screen capture has stopped. No frames are being analyzed.
Android ended screen sharing. Tap Start to begin a new session.
Screen frames are analyzed on this device, never saved or uploaded. Sharing covers your entire screen; stop before opening private content.

1. Tap Start and approve Android’s screen-sharing prompt.

2. Open the practice screen or switch to your target app. A cyan marker appears when a colored ring is detected.

3. Stop from this app, the notification, or Android’s sharing controls.
Detection and automatic throws are experimental. Rings can be missed or mistaken for other objects, and swipes can miss. Throw grades and catches are not predicted.
Analyzing your screen on this device. Tap to open controls.
Start the overlay first, then watch the cyan marker follow this ring. Tap the ring to change its color and check that touches pass through.
Animated practice ring. Tap to change its color.
Android could not open overlay settings. Enable “Display over other apps” in the app’s system settings.

Optional automatic swipes in Pokémon GO, only after you calibrate a ball position and turn Auto on. The service checks the focused app package and window bounds; it does not read or store UI text. Stop ends capture and disables future throws.
Enable Throw Assistant gestures in Android Accessibility settings.
Gesture service off — overlay guidance still works

Enable “Throw Assistant gestures” in Accessibility settings. Start capture, open a Pokémon GO encounter in portrait, tap “Set ball” in the floating controls, then tap the ball center. Tap “Auto: off” to arm up to five throws. Auto pauses when you leave the game; arm again to resume. A ring must stay steady, then disappear before another throw. Stop disables future swipes.
Adjust swipe duration from 150 to 600 milliseconds
Select the ball in the lower part of the game screen.
Ball position set. Tap Auto to arm.
Enable gesture permission, open Pokémon GO in portrait, then Set ball before turning Auto on.
